items.title: Section: Skilful Means Born of Duress — Using Legitimate Authority to Threaten Real Consequences, Then Watching Closely to Make Sure the Threat Actually Works

items.zh: 云何菩薩逼迫所生方便善巧？謂諸菩薩，或為家主、或作國王，得增上力，於自親屬、於自臣民能正教誡。如應告言：諸我親屬、諸我臣民，若於父母不知恩報，廣說乃至毀犯戒者，我當斷其常所給賜衣服、飲食，或當捶罰，或我親屬當與乖離，或我臣民當永驅擯。立一善巧機捷士夫，於彼事業常令伺察。由是因故，彼諸有情怖畏治罰，勤斷諸惡，勤修諸善。彼於修善雖無樂欲，由是方便，強逼令修。是故名為逼迫所生方便善巧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means born of duress? Bodhisattvas who, as the head of a household or the ruler of a country, hold legitimate authority, correctly instruct and warn their own family or their own subjects, declaring accordingly: "All you who are my family, all you who are my subjects — should any of you fail to recognise and repay your debt to your parents," stated in full up through violating household rules or the laws of the land, "I will cut off the clothing and food I customarily provide, or inflict punishment, or my family shall become estranged from you, or my subjects shall be permanently banished." They then appoint one genuinely skilful, alert person to keep constant watch over this matter. Through this very cause, such beings, fearing punishment, diligently abandon what is unwholesome and diligently cultivate what is wholesome. Though they have no genuine desire for cultivating wholesome conduct, through this skilful means they are forcibly compelled to undertake it. This is therefore called a bodhisattva's skilful means born of duress.

items.title: Section: Kindness and Its Repayment — the Truest Way to Repay a Debt Is Never Money, but Genuine Virtue

items.zh: 云何菩薩施恩報恩方便善巧？謂諸菩薩，先於有情隨力多少施作恩惠；或施所須，或濟厄難，或除恐怖，或會所愛，或離非愛，或療病苦，令得安樂。彼諸有情深知恩惠，欲報德者，菩薩爾時勸令修善，以受報恩。告言：汝等非餘世財來相酬遺，為大報恩；汝等若能知父母恩，恭敬供養，廣說乃至受持淨戒，如是乃名大報恩德。菩薩如是於諸有情先施恩惠，勸讚修善名大報恩；由此方便，令他於善精勤修學。是故名為施恩報恩方便善巧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means of kindness and its repayment? Bodhisattvas who first, according to their own strength and ability, extend kindness to beings — providing what is needed, rescuing from crisis, removing fear, uniting them with what they love, separating them from what they loathe, or healing their illness, bringing them ease. Should such beings, genuinely grateful, wish to repay this kindness, bodhisattvas then encourage them to take up wholesome conduct as the means of that repayment, telling them: "Do not repay me with worldly wealth of any other kind and consider that a great repayment; only if you are able to recognise your debt to your parents and honour them with reverence" — stated in full up through upholding pure precepts — "would this genuinely be called a great repayment of kindness." Bodhisattvas who thus first extend kindness to beings, and then praise and encourage wholesome conduct as its great repayment — through this very skilful means, beings are led to diligently cultivate what is wholesome. This is therefore called a bodhisattva's skilful means of kindness and its repayment.

items.title: Section: Ultimate Purity Opens — Descending From Tuṣita So That Countless Beings Might Aspire to Meet the Coming Buddha

items.zh: 云何菩薩究竟清淨方便善巧？謂諸菩薩，安住菩薩到究竟地，於菩薩道已善清淨，先現往生覩史多天眾同分中。無量有情如是念言：某名菩薩，今已生處覩史多天眾同分中，不久當下生贍部洲，證得無上正等菩提。願令我等當得值遇，非不值遇，隨是菩薩所生之處，願令我等亦當往生。如是為令無量有情生正欲樂，為多修習此欲樂故。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skilful means of ultimate purity? Bodhisattvas who, abiding at the very culmination of the bodhisattva ground, have already brought the bodhisattva path to genuine purity, first manifest rebirth within the community of Tuṣita heaven's own gods. Countless beings then reflect in this way: "This named bodhisattva has now been born within the community of Tuṣita heaven, and will, before long, descend to Jambudvīpa and attain supreme, correct awakening. May we come to genuinely encounter this buddha, and not fail to encounter them; wherever this bodhisattva is next born, may we too be born there." In this way, countless beings are led to give rise to this genuinely wholesome aspiration, cultivating it repeatedly.

items.title: Section: Birth Into a Noble Family, Then Renouncing Every Worldly Pleasure Without a Trace of Longing — Making Renunciation Itself Worthy of Reverence

items.zh: 又是菩薩，從覩史多天眾中沒，來下人間，生於高貴、或族望家。所謂王家、若國師家。棄捨世間上妙欲樂，無所顧戀，清淨出家。令諸有情起尊敬故。
items.en: Furthermore, this bodhisattva, passing from the community of Tuṣita heaven's own gods, descends into the human world, born into a family of high standing or widespread reputation — that is, a royal family or a family of court preceptors. Having renounced the world's own most exquisite pleasures without the slightest lingering attachment, this bodhisattva takes up a genuinely pure renunciation. This is done specifically so that beings everywhere come to hold this renunciation in genuine reverence.

items.title: Section: Willingly Enduring Years of Futile Austerity — So That Ascetics Devoted to Needless Suffering Might Finally Let It Go

items.zh: 又現誓受難行苦行。為令信解苦行有情捨所樂故。
items.en: Furthermore, this bodhisattva manifests a vow to undergo genuinely difficult ascetic practice. This is done specifically so that beings who place their faith and understanding in ascetic practice might release their own attachment to what they find so appealing in it.

items.title: Section: Manifesting Awakening Itself, Then Waiting for Brahmā's Own Plea Before Teaching a Single Word

items.zh: 又證無上正等菩提。令餘有情，於所同趣菩提解脫欣殊勝故。又證無上正等覺已，未為有情即說正法，待梵天王躬來啟請。為諸有情於正法所起尊敬故。作是念言：當所說法定應殊妙，故今梵王悕望世尊說是法故，躬自來請。
items.en: Furthermore, this bodhisattva attains supreme, correct awakening. This is done so that other beings who share the identical aspiration towards awakening and liberation give rise to genuine joy at its supreme excellence. Furthermore, having attained supreme, correct awakening, this buddha does not immediately teach the true dharma to beings, but waits until the great Brahmā king personally comes to formally request it. This is done so that beings give rise to genuine reverence towards the true dharma, reflecting in this way: "The teaching about to be given must surely be supremely wondrous, since even the great Brahmā king now hopes the World-Honoured One will teach it, and has come in person to make this request."

items.title: Section: Observing the World With Compassion Before Ever Turning the Wheel — Guarding Against the Claim That the Buddha's Compassion Was Merely Reactive

items.zh: 又以佛眼觀察世間，勿使有情作如是謗：但由梵王躬來啟請，敬梵王故，宣說正法，非於有情自起悲心；乃是為他之所激發，非自能了機宜可否。為欲壞彼一類有情如是邪執，先以佛眼觀察世間，然後為轉無上法輪，一切世間所未曾轉。如是更復宣說正法，制立學處。是名菩薩究竟清淨方便善巧。由此所說方便善巧，更無有餘方便善巧，在於此上若過若妙，是故說名究竟清淨。
items.en: Furthermore, the Buddha observes the world through the buddha-eye, so as to prevent beings from forming this kind of slander: "The Buddha proclaimed the true teaching only because the great Brahmā king personally came to request it, out of reverence for Brahmā, and not from any compassion arising within the Buddha's own being; the Buddha was merely provoked into it by another, and was not personally capable of judging what was actually fitting." In order to dispel this kind of mistaken grasping in certain beings, the Buddha first observes the world through the buddha-eye, and only then turns the wheel of the unsurpassed teaching, never before turned anywhere in the world. In this way the true teaching is further proclaimed, and the actual training precepts are established. This is called a bodhisattva's skilful means of ultimate purity. Among the skilful means already described, there is no further skilful means beyond or more wondrous than this; this is why it is called ultimate purity.

items.title: Section: The Eleventh Topic Closes in Full — Twelve Kinds of Skilful Means, Nothing Beyond Them Left to Add

items.zh: 如是菩薩所說六種若略若廣方便善巧，能除憎背聖教有情所有恚惱；處中住者，令其趣入；已趣入者，令其成熟；已成熟者，令得解脫。除此無有若過若增。是名菩薩方便善巧。
items.en: In this way, bodhisattvas' six kinds of skilful means, whether stated briefly or explained in full, are able to remove all hostility from beings who resent the noble teaching; to draw those who remain neutral into genuine entry; to mature those who have already entered; and to bring those already mature to actual liberation. Beyond these, there is nothing further to add and nothing further to improve upon. This is called a bodhisattva's skilful means.

blocks.text: Today closes the twelve skilful means. The last, "ultimate purity", reads the life of the Buddha as one long skilful means: each event shown for beings' sake.

"Bodhisattvas who, as head of a household or ruler of a country, hold authority, correctly instruct their family or subjects." Venerable Miào Jìng: this needs a sharp, alert person; "keeping watch" is "like a spy observing you secretly". Master Cháng Bǎi: in Buddha-recitation and meditation retreats, the monitors let even reluctant participants gain some benefit.
"Do not repay me with worldly wealth and call it great repayment; recognising your parents' kindness and honouring them … that is the great repayment."
Master Cháng Bǎi: as Maitreya now dwells in Tuṣita's inner court, where one day and night is four hundred human years.
Born into a royal or preceptor family, renouncing supreme pleasures, "so that beings come to hold it in reverence".
Master Cháng Bǎi: as Śākyamuni showed six years of austerity, so that beings fond of asceticism would let it go. Venerable Miào Jìng: in the end the Buddha abandoned austerity as well.
"So beings give rise to reverence for the true dharma, thinking: what is about to be taught must be supremely wondrous."

Lest beings say: "He taught only because Brahmā asked, not out of his own compassion." Master Cháng Bǎi: the dharma is called a wheel because it passes from one to another, rolling on; Venerable Miào Jìng: the content of the wheel is the eightfold path. 學處 here means the three trainings of precepts, concentration, and wisdom.
They remove hostility from those who resent the teaching, draw in the neutral, mature those who have entered, and liberate those already mature. Nothing beyond these twelve is needed.

subs.head: Reading the life of the Buddha

blocks.text: In Mahāyāna eyes, the great events of the Buddha's life are each a teaching. You may recognise the list from the "eight phases" (八相成道) tradition, which Day 403 mentions again in the great vows.

quiz.q: In skilful means born of duress, in what role does the bodhisattva act?
options: as head of household or king, with authority to instruct family or subjects
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas who, as head of a household or ruler of a country, hold authority, correctly instruct their family or subjects." Venerable Miào Jìng: "all you my relatives" is the head of household speaking.

quiz.q: When beings wish to repay the bodhisattva, what does the bodhisattva call "great repayment"?
options: not worldly wealth — recognising parents' kindness, honouring them, up to upholding precepts, is the great repayment
quiz.why: "Do not repay me with worldly wealth and call it great repayment; recognising your parents' kindness and honouring them, up to upholding pure precepts — that is the great repayment." Venerable Miào Jìng: "other" (餘) means worldly wealth.

quiz.q: Born into a royal or preceptor family and then renouncing, for what purpose?
options: so that beings come to hold renunciation in reverence
quiz.why: Born into a royal or preceptor family, renouncing supreme pleasures, "so that beings come to hold it in reverence." Venerable Miào Jìng: why not just skip being born there? No — this makes beings respect renunciation.

quiz.q: "Manifesting a vow of arduous asceticism" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: like Śākyamuni's six years, so that beings fond of austerity give up pointless asceticism
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: as Śākyamuni showed six years of austerity before awakening — so that beings fond of asceticism would abandon the pointless austerities they love.

quiz.q: Why does the Buddha wait for Brahmā's request before teaching?
options: so beings revere the dharma — if even Brahmā asks, the teaching must be supremely wondrous
quiz.why: "So beings give rise to reverence for the true dharma, thinking: what is about to be taught must be supremely wondrous." Venerable Miào Jìng: Brahmā coming in person shows how precious the dharma is.

quiz.q: The Buddha observes with the buddha-eye to forestall what slander? What does Venerable Miào Jìng remark?
options: lest people say he taught only because Brahmā asked, not from his own compassion; he sighs: beings are hard to save — whatever you do is right and wrong
quiz.why: Lest beings slander: "He taught only because Brahmā asked, not out of his own compassion." Venerable Miào Jìng: beings are truly hard to save — whatever is done, it's both right and wrong.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say the six kinds of skilful means accomplish?
options: remove hostility, draw in the neutral, mature those who entered, liberate the mature
quiz.why: They remove hostility from those who resent the teaching, draw the neutral in, mature those who have entered, and liberate the mature — nothing surpasses them. Venerable Miào Jìng: these are the six major sections above.
